overall: Committee violated the OML by entering executive session on June 3, 2013 for an improper purpose, using improper procedure to convene, and posting an insufficiently specific notice (intentional); ordered compliance and minutes release, and referred the matter for a hearing with a recommended $1,000 fine.

allegations.summary: Complaints said the June 3, 2013 executive session on a personnel matter was entered under an improper purpose (Purpose 7 citing G.L. c. 214, § 1B privacy).
allegations.key_passage: The Committee's invocation of the statutory right to privacy to convene this executive session was in error.

allegations.summary: Complaints said the executive session was improperly convened because a member other than the chair stated the purpose instead of the chair.
allegations.key_passage: This procedural deficiency was a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaints said the posted topic 'Personnel Matter' for the June 3, 2013 executive session was insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find the Committee's notice was insufficiently specific to comply with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25, and the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law Regulations, 940 CMR 29.00 et seq.

Following written notice to the subject of the executive session discussion, public release of the portion of the June 3, 2013 executive session minutes related to the 'Personnel Matter,' as well as any documents used by the Committee during that executive session discussion.
remedy_passage: Accordingly, we order, as a remedial measure, the public release of the portion of the June 3, 2013 executive session minutes related to the "Personnel Matter" as well as any documents used by the Committee during that executive session discussion.
